Computational Neuroscience

Our lab is involved with the development of several techniques to assist with the accurate identification and measurement of various neural structures…

 

Probabilistic tractography group analysis using cytoarchitectonic ROIs of human nuclei

 

 

 

 

 

 

As technology improves, more accurate image feature measurement techniques will be available to help identify stronger and more robust radio-genomic correlations which will lead to insights about cancer biology. Our lab has developed a semi-automatic in silico measurement pipeline to segment and interpolate the volume of various tumor compartments using a series of two dimensional MR images.

 

 

FSL: Our lab incorporates several tools available from the FSL toolset, a subset of the FMRIB Software Library hosted by Oxford University. FSL is a comprehensive library of analysis tools for FMRI, MRI and DTI brain imaging data that can be run on both Apple and PCs (For more information click here)
